claims.text: Advanced dry AMD with geographic atrophy: intravitreal every 1–2 months slows its progression (studies measured preserved retinal tissue, not visual acuity)
claims.quote: Intravitreal pegcetacoplan and intravitreal avacincaptad pegol can be used for the treatment of advanced dry AMD due to geographic atrophy (5, 6, 7). These medications inhibit the complement pathway and can slow the progression of geographic atrophy when administered every 1 to 2 months. The primary outcome used in these studies was preservation of retinal tissue, not visual acuity outcomes
